How it fits, from your side

# From one line to a boundary: what you do, and what you get.

RiskMandate writes down what your agent can reach, what you authorised, the gap, and what actually stands in the way; your own controls enforce it, and we are never in the request path. Here is the whole of it, bottom to top, with what is live and what is not yet.

**Insure it**An agent an insurer can cover, because what it can do, and what stops it, is written down and held.*in design* [more ↗](https://riskmandate.ai/insurance.html)
**Authorise it**A licence to operate: an owner, a behaviour policy and an expiry, with autonomy earned a level at a time.*template* [more ↗](https://riskmandate.ai/licence-to-operate.html)
**Make a row a boundary**A Process Behaviour Policy, held by the Linux kernel: SHarness, open source. Today for the processes an agent starts, on Linux.*experiments* [more](/demos/sharness/index.md)
**Write down the whole gap**Your Agent Behaviour Policy: the grant measured, the mandate in your words, the gap derived, a barrier on every row. In an encrypted vault you hold the keys to.*live* [more ↗](https://riskmandate.ai/abp.html)
**Hold them in the harness**For Claude Code, the starter pack: four lines and four hooks, from expectation to setting.*live* [more](/policies/starter/index.md)
**Pick the rules**riskmandate.ai's 24 rules, one worry and one line each, each with an honest note on what holds it.*live* [more ↗](https://riskmandate.ai/rules/)
**Try one line**Six examples in Claude or ChatGPT, in your browser: ask, paste one line, ask again. Five minutes, free.*live* [more](/examples/index.md)

Open model: [abp.sgit.ai ↗](https://abp.sgit.ai/) · Open enforcer: [sharness.ai ↗](https://sharness.ai/) · Your vaults: sgit, you hold the keys

<a id="steps"></a>

## Your first agent, in steps

1. **S0 · In, with credit.**

£50 of credit for reading this site, and the six examples. Nothing to install.

2. **S1 · One agent named.**

One agent you actually run, in one deployment, matched to the nearest of sixteen published examples.

3. **S2 · Its grant, measured.**

What it can reach, from its deployment and credentials: a prompt you run, or the documentation where you cannot.

4. **S3 · Its mandate, in your words.**

What you want it to do, what you do not, and what nobody mentioned. The correction is the elicitation.

5. **S4 · The gap, and the first finding.**

The rows it can reach that nobody authorised, and the one that surprises you.

6. **S5 · Hooks and boundaries.**

The rows the harness can hold become hooks; the rows that need a boundary get one, in your gateway, your IAM, or a kernel policy.

7. **S6 · The usage moment.**

In your words: what it is worth, and what a fair price is.

<a id="levels"></a>

## Four levels, one document

| Level | What you get | Price |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · The pack | Every file of the ABP, downloaded | £10 |

| 3 · Corrected for your situation | You run the measuring prompt and send the grant and mandate; we correct it, with a note of what changed and why | £500 · free for early users |
| 4 · Reviewed and signed | Two half-hour sessions, then a sign-off with a name and a date | £1,500 |
